chapter.li: Verse12 And it came to pass, in those days, that he went out into a mountain to pray, and continued all night in prayer to God. VerseEnd Verse13 And when it was day, he called his disciples. And of them he chose twelve, whom he also named apostles: VerseEnd Verse14 Simon, whom he also named Peter, and Andrew his brother, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew, VerseEnd Verse15 Matthew and Thomas, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon called Zelotes, VerseEnd Verse16 and Judas the brother of James, and Judas Iscariot, who also was the traitor. VerseEnd Verse17 And he came down with them and stood in the plain, and the company of his disciples, and a great multitude of people out of all Judea and Jerusalem, and from the sea coasts of Tyre and Sidon, who came to hear him and to be healed of their diseases, VerseEnd Verse18 and they who were vexed with unclean spirits; and they were healed. VerseEnd Verse19 And the whole multitude sought to touch him, for there went virtue out of him and healed them all. VerseEnd
Verse20 And he lifted up his eyes on his disciples and said, Blessed are the poor, for theirs is the kingdom of God. VerseEnd
Verse21 Blessed are they who hunger now, for they shall be filled.
Blessed are they who weep now, for they shall laugh. VerseEnd

Verse22 Blessed are you when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you from among them, and shall reproach you, and cast out your name as evil, for the Son of Man’s sake. VerseEnd Verse23 Rejoice in that day and leap for joy, for behold, your reward shall be great in Heaven, for in the like manner did their fathers unto the prophets. VerseEnd
Verse24 But woe unto you that are rich, for you have received your consolation. VerseEnd
Verse25 Woe unto you who are full, for you shall hunger.
Woe unto you who laugh now, for you shall mourn and weep. VerseEnd
Verse26 Woe unto you when all men shall speak well of you, for so did their fathers to the false prophets. VerseEnd

Verse27 But I say unto you who hear my words, love your enemies, do good to them who hate you, VerseEnd Verse28 bless them who curse you, and pray for them who falsely accuse you VerseEnd Verse29 and persecute you. And unto him who smites you on the cheek, offer also the other. Or in other words, it is better to offer the other than to revile again. And he who takes away your cloak, forbid not to take your coat also, for it is better that you suffer your enemy to take these things than to contend with him. Truly I say unto you, your Heavenly Father, who sees in secret, shall bring that wicked one into judgment. VerseEnd Verse30 Therefore, give to every man who asks of you, and of him who takes away your goods, ask them not again. VerseEnd

Verse31 And as you desire that men should do to you, do also to them likewise. VerseEnd Verse32 For if you love only those who love you, what reward have you? For sinners also do even the same. VerseEnd Verse33 And if you do good to them who only do good to you, what reward have you? For sinners also do even the same. VerseEnd Verse34 And if you lend to them of whom you hope to receive, what reward have you? For sinners also lend to sinners, to receive as much again. VerseEnd Verse35 But love your enemies, and do good, and lend hoping for nothing again, and your reward shall be great, and you shall be the children of the Highest. For he is kind unto the unthankful and the evil. VerseEnd Verse36 Be therefore merciful as your Father also is merciful. VerseEnd Verse37 Judge not and you shall not be judged. Condemn not and you shall not be condemned. Forgive and you shall be forgiven. VerseEnd Verse38 Give and it shall be given unto you — good measure, pressed down and shaken together, and running over shall men give into your bosom. For with the same measure that you mete, it shall be measured to you again. VerseEnd

Verse39 And he spoke a parable unto them: Can the blind lead the blind? Shall they not both fall into the ditch? VerseEnd Verse40 A disciple is not above his master, but everyone that is perfect shall be as his master. VerseEnd Verse41 And why do you behold the speck which is in your brother’s eye, but perceive not the beam which is in your own eye? VerseEnd Verse42 Again, how can you say to your brother, Let me pull out the speck that is in your eye, when you yourself behold not the beam which is in your own eye? You hypocrite, cast out first the beam, out of your own eye, and then shall you see clearly to pull out the speck which is in your brother’s eye. VerseEnd Verse43 For a good tree brings not forth corrupt fruit, neither does a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit, VerseEnd Verse44 for every tree is known by his own fruit. For of thorns men do not gather figs, nor of a bramble bush do they gather grapes. VerseEnd Verse45 A good man, out of the good treasure of his heart, brings forth that which is good; and an evil man, out of the evil treasure of his heart, brings forth that which is evil. For of the abundance of the heart, his mouth speaks. VerseEnd

Verse46 And why do you call me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say? VerseEnd Verse47 Whoever comes to me and hears my sayings and does them, I will show you to whom he is like. VerseEnd Verse48 He is like a man who built a house, and dug deep, and laid the foundation on a rock. And when the flood arose, the stream beat vehemently upon that house and could not shake it, for it was founded upon a rock. VerseEnd Verse49 But he who hears and does not is like a man that, without a foundation, built a house upon the earth, against which the stream did beat vehemently, and immediately it fell; and the ruin of that house was great. VerseEnd

LEChapter7 Verse1 Now when he had ended all these sayings in the audience of the people, he entered into Capernaum. VerseEnd Verse2 And a certain centurion’s servant, who was dear unto him, was sick and about to die. VerseEnd Verse3 And when he heard of Jesus, he sent unto him the elders of the Jews, imploring him that he would come and heal his servant. VerseEnd Verse4 And when they came to Jesus, they implored him earnestly, saying that he was worthy, for whom he should do this: VerseEnd Verse5 For he loves our nation, and he has built us a synagogue. VerseEnd Verse6 Then Jesus went with them. And when he was now not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to him, saying unto him, Lord, trouble not yourself. For I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof; VerseEnd Verse7 wherefore, neither did I think myself worthy to come unto you. But say the word and my servant shall be healed, VerseEnd Verse8 for I also am a man set under authority, having under me soldiers; and I say unto one, Go, and he goes, and to another, Come, and he comes, and to my servant, Do this, and he does it. VerseEnd Verse9 When Jesus heard these things, he marveled at him, and turned himself about and said unto the people who followed him, I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel. VerseEnd Verse10 And they who were sent, returning to the house, found the servant whole who had been sick. VerseEnd

Verse11 And it came to pass, the day after, that he went into a city called Nain. And many of his disciples went with him, and many people. VerseEnd Verse12 Now when he came near to the gate of the city, behold, there was a dead man carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow. And many people of the city were with her. VerseEnd Verse13 And now the Lord saw her, and he had compassion on her, and he said unto her, Weep not. VerseEnd Verse14 And he came and touched the bier, and they who bore it stood still. And he said, Young man, I say unto you, arise. VerseEnd Verse15 And he who was dead sat up and began to speak. And he delivered him to his mother. VerseEnd Verse16 And there came a fear on all, and they glorified God, saying that a great prophet is risen up among us, and that God has visited his people. VerseEnd Verse17 And this rumor of him went forth throughout all Judea and throughout all the region round about. VerseEnd

Verse18 And the disciples of John showed him of all these things. VerseEnd Verse19 And John, calling two of his disciples, sent them to Jesus, saying, Are you he that should come? Or do we look for another? VerseEnd Verse20 When the men had come unto him, they said, John the Baptist has sent us unto you, saying, Are you he who should come? Or do we look for another? VerseEnd Verse21 And in the same hour, he cured many of infirmities, and plagues, and of evil spirits, and unto many blind he gave sight. VerseEnd Verse22 Then Jesus answering said unto them, Go your way and tell John what things you have seen and heard: how that the blind see, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and to the poor the gospel is preached. VerseEnd Verse23 And blessed are they who shall not be offended in me. VerseEnd

Verse24 And when the messengers of John had departed, he began to speak unto the people concerning John, What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken with the wind? VerseEnd Verse25 Or a man clothed in soft raiment? Behold, they who are gorgeously appareled and live delicately are in kings’ courts. VerseEnd Verse26 But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yea, I say unto you, and much more than a prophet. VerseEnd Verse27 This is the one of whom it is written: Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who shall prepare your way before you. VerseEnd Verse28 For I say unto you, among those who are born of women, there is not a greater prophet than John the Baptist. But he who is least in the kingdom of God is greater than he. VerseEnd Verse29 And all the people who heard him, and the publicans, justified God, being baptized with the baptism of John. VerseEnd Verse30 But the Pharisees and lawyers rejected the counsel of God against themselves, being not baptized of him. VerseEnd

Verse31 And the Lord said, Unto what then shall I liken the men of this generation? And to what are they like? VerseEnd Verse32 They are like unto children sitting in the marketplace, and calling one to another, and saying, We have piped for you and you have not danced. We have mourned for you and you have not wept. VerseEnd Verse33 For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, He has a devil. VerseEnd Verse34 The Son of Man has come eating and drinking, and you say, Behold a gluttonous man and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. VerseEnd Verse35 But Wisdom is justified of all her children. VerseEnd

Verse36 And one of the Pharisees desired of him that he would eat with him. And he went into the Pharisee’s house, and he sat down to a meal. VerseEnd Verse37 And behold, a woman in the city, who was a sinner, when she knew that Jesus sat at a meal in the Pharisee’s house, brought an alabaster box of ointment, VerseEnd Verse38 and stood at his feet weeping, and began to wash his feet with tears, and did wipe them with the hairs of her head, and kissed his feet, and anointed them with the ointment. VerseEnd Verse39 Now when the Pharisee who had bidden him saw this, he spoke within himself, saying, This man, if he were a prophet, would have known who or what manner of woman this is who touches him, for she is a sinner. VerseEnd

Verse40 And Jesus answering said unto him, Simon, I have somewhat to say unto you. And he said, Master, say on. VerseEnd Verse41 And Jesus said, There was a certain creditor who had two debtors. The one owed five hundred pence, and the other fifty. VerseEnd Verse42 And when he found they had nothing to pay, he freely forgave them both. Tell me, therefore, which of them will love him most? VerseEnd Verse43 Simon answered and said, I suppose the man to whom he forgave most. And he said unto him, You have rightly judged. VerseEnd

Verse44 And he turned to the woman and said unto Simon, Do you see this woman? I entered into your house. You gave me no water for my feet, but she has washed my feet with tears, and wiped them with the hairs of her head. VerseEnd Verse45 You gave me no kiss, but this woman, since the time I came in, has not ceased to kiss my feet. VerseEnd Verse46 My head with oil you did not anoint, but this woman has anointed my feet with ointment. VerseEnd Verse47 Wherefore, I say unto you, her sins, which are many, are forgiven, for she loved much. But to whom little is forgiven, the same loves little. VerseEnd Verse48 And he said unto her, Your sins are forgiven. VerseEnd Verse49 And they who sat at a meal with him began to say within themselves, Who is this that forgives sins also? VerseEnd Verse50 And he said to the woman, Your faith has saved you. Go in peace. VerseEnd
